subject: Pricing floor, PO requirements and invoice cadence for CoreMed pilot
messages:
From: Dana Liu <dana.liu@coremed.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: CoreMed Procurement <procurement@coremed.com>
Date: Tue, 5 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: PO requirements / invoice cadence for the pilot

Hi Marcus,

Thanks again for the demo last week — team was impressed with latency and the cost breakdown. Procurement asked me to flag a few constraints before we can issue a formal PO:

- PO needs SKU-level line items for each license tier (we need an itemized charge for the enterprise and add-on tokens).
- Net terms: standard for us is Net60. Can you accept Net60 for the pilot?
- Invoice cadence: we prefer monthly invoices rather than quarterly.
- One small ask: would you be able to include a 2% prompt-pay discount if we pay within 15 days?

Also attaching our PO template for your legal/billing team to review. If any of the above is a blocker we need to know before the end of the week so we can align internal approvers.

Best,
Dana Liu
Sr. Procurement Manager
CoreMed Systems
Attachment: CoreMed_PO_Template.pdf
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Dana Liu <dana.liu@coremed.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 5 May 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: PO requirements / invoice cadence for the pilot

Dana —

Appreciate the clear list. We can accommodate most of this, with a couple of clarifying items:

1) SKU-level lines: yes — we can produce itemized line items that match your template. Could you confirm the exact SKU labels you expect (e.g., ENTERPRISE_MONTHLY, TOKEN_OVERAGE)? We’ll map our product codes.

2) Net60: we generally price with Net30, but for annual/committed pilots we can accept Net60 on a case-by-case basis. Need finance sign-off.

3) Monthly invoices: fine. We will change the cadence on the billing mandate.

4) Prompt-pay discount: we can offer a tiered discount tied to commitment. Example proposal:
   - No commitment: standard list price, Net30.
   - 12-month commitment (minimum $120k ARR): 12% off list, Net60 accepted, monthly invoices.
   - 24-month commitment: 18% off list, Net60, monthly invoices.

If you prefer the 2% for 15-day payment specifically (without committing volume), we can make that available as a limited concession but it will not stack with the commitment discount.

I’ve attached a draft License_Proposal_Q3.xlsx with the tiered pricing mapped to your PO template assumptions. I’ll loop in finance and sales ops internally to confirm Net60.

Next step: can you confirm whether your PO will include the Full Legal Entity name and Tax ID on the header (we need that for invoice routing)? Also please confirm billing contact name/email.

Thanks,
Marcus
Director, Sales — Enterprise
Redwood Inference
Attachment: License_Proposal_Q3.xlsx
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 5 May 2026 14:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: PO requirements / invoice cadence for the pilot

Folks — forwarding CoreMed’s PO template and their asks below. Key asks: SKU-level lines, Net60, monthly invoices, optional 2% prompt-pay.

Quoted original message:
> From: Dana Liu <dana.liu@coremed.com>
> Date: Tue, 5 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
> Subject: PO requirements / invoice cadence for the pilot
>
> - PO needs SKU-level line items for each license tier
> - Net60
> - Monthly invoices
> - 2% prompt-pay for payment within 15 days

Ben — can finance confirm Net60 on a 12-month committed pilot at the discount levels above? We typically allow extended terms on committed ARR but want to be explicit about the exposure. Please also confirm whether we can make the 2% short-pay discount available as a stand-alone concession (no commitment) or make it only applicable if they prepay.

Kimberly — sales ops: if we accept SKU mapping, will our billing system accept the CoreMed PO template fields as-is? Any required fields that would cause rejection?

Vanessa — can you weigh in on the negotiation posture? My read is: offer 12% for 12 months (minimum $120k), accept Net60, monthly invoices; offer 2% prompt-pay for customers that cannot commit, but flag that it doesn’t stack with the commitment discount.

Thanks —
Marcus

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Dana Liu <dana.liu@coremed.com>
Date: Wed, 6 May 2026 16:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: PO requirements / invoice cadence for the pilot

Marcus / team / Dana —

Finance reviewed the ask. We can approve Net60 for the pilot if we have either: (a) a signed 12-month commitment at >= $120k ARR with a 12% discount, or (b) a 24-month commitment at >= $200k ARR with an 18% discount. Those commits should be captured in the SOW or Master Services Agreement and referenced on the PO.

Operational notes: monthly invoices are acceptable. We will need the PO to include the following fields exactly as formatted to avoid AP rejection:
- Billing legal entity (Full legal name)
- Billing address and Tax ID / VAT number
- PO number (alphanumeric)
- Invoice remit-to email and ACH wire instructions (we’ll provide a template wire stub)

On the 2% early-pay discount: we can offer it as a stand-alone limited concession for one-off pilots but it cannot be combined with the multi-month commitment discounts. If CoreMed wants both stacked, finance requires an escrow or prepayment for the difference.

If that aligns, Marcus please send back a short Commercial Summary (1 page) that we can append to the PO so procurement has the commit wording to put into their system.

Ben Carter
Head of Finance — Redwood Inference
Attachment: (none)
